instruction_authority: org/platform policy > current-task human > project/path instructions > adopted suite > user-global > third-party skills (except vendor API how-to) > model taste
implementation_convention: approved task design > nearest file > package > repository > suite default
bootstrap: **Bootstrap (every task):** this file → protocol → only relevant guides → STATUS if present → test/lint baseline → plan if non-trivial → edit.
hard_items: destructive data, new auth, new deployable, true product ambiguity
always_ask_suite_extra: and before rewriting author-native guide voice without review

routes.need: Protocol (start, ask vs decide, done, handoff)
Git flow / parallel agents / subagent briefs

skills.description: Use for any code writing or editing: code shape, smells, naming, decomposition, error handling style, post-code style check. Applies to nearly every code task.
Use when shaping a system: greenfield layout, engines/modules vs deployables, folder structure, new service/package/repo proposals, shared code policy.
Use when choosing or discussing language, framework, or storage: greenfield stack proposals, new major dependency, storage selection, stack bans. Greenfield picks are never autonomous.
Use for schema and data work: tables, migrations, keys, nullability, invariants, money and time representation.
Use for wire contracts: HTTP endpoints, events, DTOs, API versioning, wire error shapes, internal transport.
Use when adding or changing logs, metrics, traces, DB health, runtime data health/lineage, or early APM setup.
Use for any behavior change, bugfix, or test work: what to test, TDD, repro tests, characterization pins for untested legacy code, factories, flakes. Every bugfix gets a test.
Use when touching auth boundaries, permissions, PII, secrets, IDOR risks, or supply chain concerns.
Use for rollout work: feature flags, expand/contract migrations, rollback planning, deploy safety. Human ships prod.
